current_leader.name: Card authorization integrity-fee prevention engine
current_leader.state_transition: approved authorization -> capture/reversal absent as scheme deadline approaches -> combine PSP lifecycle state with merchant fulfillment state -> recommend CAPTURE/REVERSE/NO ACTION before integrity-fee trigger -> reconcile avoided fee
current_leader.why_survived: 2026 fee schedules confirm deterministic material penalties: Mastercard processing-integrity fees at 0.452% with $0.113 minimum in Moneris' schedule, plus a 0.0339% authorization-validity fee for final transactions cleared 72-168 hours after authorization. Visa US misuse-of-authorization is $0.15 per non-compliant transaction. The wedge can remain read-only. Competitive whitespace was reduced because Tagada already tracks cross-processor authorization expiry and can auto-capture/re-authorize, though no exact merchant-side fulfillment-aware stale-authorization reversal-before-integrity-fee product was found.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: Moneris publishes 2026 Mastercard Processing Integrity Final Auth and Not Reversed/Cleared Preauthorization fees at 0.452% with a $0.113 minimum; Moneris/TD publish the new 0.0339% authorization-validity fee for 72-168 hour clearing; Visa US misuse fee is $0.15. Tagada's cross-processor capture-window monitoring is the strongest new competitive threat.
current_leader.closest_threat: Tagada payment orchestration, Shopify capture-at-fulfillment/expiry warnings, PSP-native capture/expiry behavior, and broad scheme-fee intelligence products including CardTraq, SchemeSense and Recivr. The exact fulfillment-aware reversal-before-fee control remains unconfirmed.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read authorization/capture/reversal webhooks plus order/fulfillment state; maintain scheme/MCC/region deadline rules; output REVERSE NOW, CAPTURE NOW, or NO ACTION with projected avoided fee; keep execution merchant-confirmed.
current_leader.monetization: Per prevented-fee event or capped share of reconciled integrity fees avoided; low monitoring fee only after observed exposure exceeds cost.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Incidence per merchant is still unquantified, and orchestration platforms may already absorb the exact control for sophisticated merchants.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify integrity-fee dollars per 100k authorizations by delayed-capture vertical and search exact automatic reversal-before-scheme-deadline competitors. Demote/reject if incidence is low or orchestration already performs the exact reversal decision.

recent_cross_family_findings: Card authorization integrity-fee prevention remains leader but was demoted 50->49 because Tagada already provides cross-processor authorization-window monitoring and auto-capture/re-authorization.

2026 fee evidence strengthens the leakage math: Mastercard processing-integrity fees can be 0.452% with a $0.113 minimum, and a separate 0.0339% authorization-validity fee now applies to some final transactions cleared 72-168 hours after authorization.

Merchant card-network behavior-fee sentinel promoted as a 47/60 adjacent hypothesis using Visa Data Quality, Mastercard excessive-authorization/MAC and integrity thresholds, but remedies sometimes require transaction-path control and broad scheme-fee competitors exist.
Restaurant/service no-show fee recovery rejected because booking products already automatically charge stored cards on no-show status.
Commercial energy demand-charge peak optimization rejected because exact meter/battery/control products already forecast peaks and automatically dispatch/load-shift.
Off-cycle payroll batching remains 43/60; UKG publicly lists a $55 off-cycle payroll fee, but economics and payroll constraints remain weaker.
Creator payout-fee batching is weak (~41/60): fees are real, but optimization is usually simple self-serve arithmetic around cash timing.
New rule: measure incidence separately from fee rate; deterministic penalty magnitude alone does not establish a large recoverable pool.
